senses.gloss: M., the owner of an idolatrous temple (<cite ref="Judges 17:12">Jud. XVII</cite>).
units: <cite ref="Esther Rabbah 7:11">Esth. R. to III, 7</cite> <he>צלם מ׳</he>; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 103b:15">Snh. 103ᵇ</cite> <he>פסלו של מ׳</he> the image put up by M.; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 103b:15">ib.</cite> <he>עשן פסל מ׳</he> the smoke rising from the sacrifices to the image &c.—
<cite ref="Shevuot 35b:6">Shebu. 35ᵇ</cite> <he>כל שמות … במ׳ תול</he> all divine names mentioned in connection with M. (Jud. l. c.) are profane (not names of the Lord).
<cite ref="Pesachim 117a:10">Pes. 117ᵃ</cite> <he>פיסלו של מ׳ עומד בבכי וכ׳</he> with Micah’s image at Bekhi, the Israelites should have sung the Hallel?—
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 41:1">Ex. R. s. 41</cite>; a. fr.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 10:2">Lev. R. s. 10</cite> <he>שלחתי את מ׳ וכ׳</he> I sent M. and they smote him.
<cite ref="Makkot 24a:25">Macc. 24ᵃ</cite> <he>בא מ׳ והעמירן וכ׳</he> M. came and based all the laws of the Torah on three principles; a. e.
